name: Macrocystic Lymphatic Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Lymphatic Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of soft, compressible, painless cystic mass typically located in the cervicofacial region
Ultrasound and MRI showing multiloculated cystic lesions with macrocystic components (>2 cm cysts)
Histological confirmation showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation plus confirmatory imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is supportive but not always required if imaging and clinical features are definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically located in the neck or axilla
Cysts usually larger than 2 cm in diameter
searchTerms: large cystic lesions with multiple compartments

common.symptomName: Cosmetic deformity due to mass effect
Respiratory distress due to airway compression
common.notes: More common in large cervicofacial lesions
searchTerms: trouble breathing due to airway compression

occasional.symptomName: Infection or cellulitis of the lesion
Pain or tenderness due to secondary infection or hemorrhage
searchTerms: pain from infected or bleeding lesion
discomfort caused by lesion infection or bleeding

occasional.notes: May affect swallowing or neck mobility

rare.symptomName: Lymphorrhea or leakage of lymphatic fluid

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests unless secondary infection present
Possible elevated inflammatory markers if infected
imaging: Ultrasound showing multiloculated cystic lesions with thin septations
MRI demonstrating macrocystic lymphatic malformation with fluid-filled cysts >2 cm
CT scan may be used to assess extent and relation to adjacent structures
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence common
other: Histopathology showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells
Fluid analysis may show lymphocyte-rich fluid

distinguishingFeatures: Compressible but less fluctuant than lymphatic malformations
Located along anterior border of sternocleidomastoid muscle
No multiloculated cystic architecture on imaging
Rapid growth in infancy followed by involution

redFlags: Rapid increase in size causing airway obstruction
Signs of infection such as erythema, warmth, and fever
Neurological deficits due to mass effect on adjacent nerves
references: Wassef M, Blei F, Adams D, et al. Vascular Anomalies Classification: Recommendations From the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.
Smith MC, et al. Lymphatic Malformations: Diagnosis and Management. J Pediatr Surg. 2019;54(11):2347-2353.
